summary: Returns the value after checking that it is not a scalar.
description: A primitive that carries a single value: string, number, boolean, symbol or bigint. `null` and `undefined` are primitives too, but they carry no value and do not qualify.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, with a scalar excluded from its type.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireNonScalar({}); // => {}
requireNonScalar([]); // => []
requireNonScalar("abc"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonScalar(1); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
